harness.independence: Reference canonicalizer/hasher/merkle written from the written protocol rules only (ADR-005, arch doc §6.1); zero imports from the SUT in src/reference. The SUT is loaded exclusively via src/sut.ts from a frozen snapshot.

capture.note: Verbatim copy of Builder A's protocol-schema source at capture time. The harness imports ONLY this snapshot; the live tree is never loaded by tests.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander ruling R9 (PROOF TARGET BINDING), 2026-09-17: V1 proof_binding MUST bind at least intent_hash + milestone_id + milestone_revision + evidence_root + policy_hash. A proof must prove the result belongs to THIS specific milestone. Not deferrable to S1.
freeze_blockers.rationale: R9 PROOF TARGET BINDING: proof_binding must be computed over intent_hash, milestone_id, bundle_id, milestone_revision, evidence_root and policy_hash. [S-R9] FAILs any SUT whose binding does not separate both proof targets.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander OQ-5 disposition, 2026-09-17/18: remove '@' from SubjectRef id charset in V1.
freeze_blockers.rationale: SubjectRef rejects '@' (OQ-5): no lookalike principal ids.
UUID canonical form is lowercase hyphenated text, version-agnostic; uppercase and non-UUID text must be rejected.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series, 2026-09-18: sealed round-trip not holding -> FAIL.
freeze_blockers.rationale: R10 SEALED ROUND-TRIP: all five first-class hashable objects (IntentContract, EvidenceArtifact, EvidenceBundle, VerificationDecision, SettlementInstruction) must seal -> JSON text round-trip -> re-seal idempotently and reject a wrong declared content_hash.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series, 2026-09-18: multiple assets in one Settlement -> FAIL.
freeze_blockers.rationale: One SettlementInstruction carries exactly one asset; mixed-asset outputs must be rejected.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series, 2026-09-18: amount scale beyond asset.decimals -> FAIL.
freeze_blockers.rationale: Output amount scale (decimal places) must not exceed the referenced asset's decimals.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series, 2026-09-18: budget cap > total -> FAIL.
freeze_blockers.rationale: Budget execution_cap must not exceed total.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series, 2026-09-18: lone surrogate entering IPC-JSON-1 -> FAIL.
freeze_blockers.rationale: IPC-JSON-1 rejects lone surrogates: strings must be Unicode scalar text.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series + PR #3 round 5: ID uniqueness is executable spec; old GAP blocker deduplicated into this assertion.
freeze_blockers.rationale: criterion_id and constraint_id are unique within their Intent.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series + PR #3 round 5: SEALED merkle enforcement is executable spec.
freeze_blockers.rationale: A SEALED bundle is rejected unless its merkle_root equals the recomputed root of its artifact set.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series + PR #3 round 5: canonical decimal is executable spec.
freeze_blockers.rationale: Amounts are canonical Decimal V1 minimal form: '150'/'15.5' accepted; '1.10'/'0.00'/'-0'/'150.0' rejected.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander R-series + PR #3 round 5: settlement sum invariant is executable spec.
freeze_blockers.rationale: total_amount equals the exact (BigInt) sum of outputs.amount.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander OQ-1 / IPC-JSON-1 freeze, 2026-09-18: canonical profile named IPC-JSON-1; keys must already be NFC.
freeze_blockers.rationale: IPC-JSON-1 R3: object keys must ALREADY be in Normalization Form C; non-NFC keys are rejected, never silently normalized (silent normalization created duplicate-key ambiguity).

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander freeze, docs/TRUST-CHAIN.md @ e28a22e (2026-09-18): exact wire contracts are normative for G1; Milestone identity is (intent_hash, milestone_id, milestone_revision).
freeze_blockers.rationale: MilestoneV1 EXACT WIRE (B-TC1): exported as MilestoneSchema; field-name set EXACTLY {schema_version, milestone_id, intent_hash, milestone_revision, criterion_ids, verification_policy_hash, settlement_policy_hash, allocation, content_hash?, signature?}; literal 'milestone.v1'; revision >= 1; criterion_ids non-empty/unique/order-significant; allocation scale <= asset.decimals; every required field feeds the digest; domain pinned to intent-protocol/v1/milestone; seal round-trip idempotent. Semantic aliases are not conforming.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander freeze, docs/TRUST-CHAIN.md @ e28a22e (2026-09-18): receipt wire/hash object and deterministic bindings are frozen in G1; formation logic is S1.
freeze_blockers.rationale: OutcomeReceiptV1 EXACT WIRE (B-TC2): exported as OutcomeReceiptSchema; field-name set EXACTLY {schema_version, receipt_id, intent_hash, milestone_id, milestone_revision, evidence_root, verification_policy_hash, decision_hashes, accepted_result, issued_at, content_hash?, signature?}; literals 'outcome-receipt.v1' / 'ACCEPTED'; decision_hashes non-empty, unique, strictly lexicographically ascending; every required field feeds the digest; domain pinned to intent-protocol/v1/outcome-receipt; seal round-trip idempotent. A receipt is the protocol-accepted outcome; a decision is only a verifier assertion.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander freeze, docs/TRUST-CHAIN.md @ e28a22e (2026-09-18): settlement is authorized only from an accepted OutcomeReceipt; a raw VerificationDecision / proof_binding is never settlement authority.
freeze_blockers.rationale: SETTLEMENT IS RECEIPT-GATED (B-TC3): SettlementInstructionV1 must carry EXACTLY {schema_version, settlement_id, escrow_ref, outcome_receipt_hash, nonce, outputs, total_amount, expires_at?, content_hash?}; the authority fields decision_id and proof_binding are FORBIDDEN and unrepresentable; a settlement without outcome_receipt_hash is rejected; the superseded decision-gated wire must NOT parse; one-asset/scale/exact-sum rules hold on the receipt-gated wire.

freeze_blockers.ruling: Commander freeze, docs/TRUST-CHAIN.md @ e28a22e (2026-09-18): settlement idempotency key binds the receipt, with explicit 0x00 terminator before the fixed-width u64be nonce; same three-way discipline as R9.
freeze_blockers.rationale: SETTLEMENT KEY FROZEN BYTE PROTOCOL (B-TC4): settlement_key = SHA256("intent-protocol/v1/settlement-key" || 0x00 || outcome_receipt_hash[32] || UTF8(escrow_ref) || 0x00 || nonce_u64be[8]). Three independent implementations must agree byte-exactly: the TS oracle (src/reference/hash.ts), the Python KAT (scripts/kat-settlement-key.py via vectors/settlement-key-vector.json, whose expected was computed by Python first), and the SUT. A SUT computing the superseded proof_binding-keyed, domain-less preimage FAILS.

summary.freeze_declaration: NONE — a machine READY status is never an automatic G1 PASS. This report does not declare the schema frozen; freeze authority and the final signature belong to the Commander. 31 FAIL findings, 25 UNKNOWN entries; freeze blockers: 17 OPEN / 0 DISPOSITIONED.

attack_surfaces.title: NFC key-collision produces duplicate-key canonical JSON
attack_surfaces.detail: canonicalize({NFC 'é': 1, NFD 'e'+U+0301: 2}) emits '{"é":1,"é":2}' — invalid, ambiguous canonical text. A second implementation (or JSON.parse) collapses the keys, so the same canonical bytes can be re-read as a different object than the one that was hashed. The independent reference rejects this case.

attack_surfaces.title: -0 silently canonicalizes to 0 against the frozen spec text
attack_surfaces.detail: Spec header rule 4 says -0 is rejected; the implementation maps -0 -> 0. Two distinct JS values share one canonical form; a strict cross-language implementation following the written rule will refuse objects the TS implementation accepts (and hash differently on any value it does emit).

attack_surfaces.title: Schema admits values the canonicalizer rejects (unhashable-but-valid objects)
attack_surfaces.detail: Criterion.threshold uses z.number().int() (accepts 2^53, 1e308) while canonicalization requires safe integers; U64-as-string regex accepts 2^64 while u64be() throws. A schema-valid Intent/Settlement can exist that can never be sealed — parsers in other languages will disagree about whether the object is acceptable at all.

attack_surfaces.title: Timestamp format is shape-checked, not calendrically validated
attack_surfaces.detail: '2026-13-45T99:99:99.999Z' passes TimestampSchema despite being invalid RFC 3339. Cross-language timestamp parsers (strict RFC 3339) will reject objects the TS layer accepted, splitting the hash universe.

attack_surfaces.title: No canonical decimal form
attack_surfaces.detail: Amounts like '1.0' / '1.00' / '1' / '-0' are distinct canonical strings for the same economic value. Any component that normalizes decimals before hashing (or after) will disagree with one that does not. Settlement amounts are the highest-value instance.

attack_surfaces.title: Duplicate-key raw JSON collapses last-wins before canonicalization
attack_surfaces.detail: '{"a":1,"a":2}' and '{"a":2}' hash identically. Byte-level audit of evidence text diverges from hash-level identity; a malicious producer can include decoy keys that vanish in the hash.

attack_surfaces.title: Identifier uniqueness is unenforced (criterion_id, constraint_id, bundle_id reuse)
attack_surfaces.detail: Same-id different-content criteria are representable; the same bundle_id can seal two different artifact sets. Downstream resolution by id becomes attacker-choosable.

attack_surfaces.title: Cross-object references are free-floating
attack_surfaces.detail: decisions bind fabricated intent_hash/evidence_root; settlements bind dangling decision_id; bundles bind nonexistent runs. Nothing in the delivered layer enforces the §15.1 north-star chain (Receipt -> Settlement -> Decision -> Bundle -> Run -> Intent). The proof_binding construction is sound, but its INPUTS are unauthenticated at this layer.

attack_surfaces.title: SEALED bundle state does not imply a correct merkle_root
attack_surfaces.detail: The bundle invariant checks presence, not consistency: a SEALED bundle with a fabricated merkle_root parses. Detection requires every consumer to recompute merkleRoot(artifact_hashes) — cheap, but currently nothing mandates it.

attack_surfaces.title: Domain/version separation relies on 0x00 exclusion, not length prefixing
attack_surfaces.detail: hash_input = domain||0x00||version||0x00||canonical is injective only because (a) domain/version literals are frozen and 0x00-free and (b) canonical JSON escapes control characters. Any future domain string containing U+0000, or a non-JSON-escaping canonicalizer, breaks the separation. A length-prefixed design would not depend on both invariants.

attack_surfaces.title: Unicode strategy diverges from RFC 8785/JCS while claiming compatibility
attack_surfaces.detail: RESOLVED IN SPEC: the canonical profile is now formally named IPC-JSON-1 (OQ-1) and intentionally diverges from raw RFC 8785/JCS: string VALUES are NFC-normalized, KEYS must already be NFC, and lone surrogates are rejected. Residual hazard: this divergence is deliberate, so a strict JCS implementation still produces different bytes — cross-implementation consumers must implement IPC-JSON-1, not JCS. U+2028/U+2029 remain raw (valid JSON, JS-source-illegal).

attack_surfaces.title: Delivered scope is a moving subset of the documented protocol
attack_surfaces.detail: Arch doc §6/§7 document 10+ object kinds and 6 state machines; the delivered snapshot contains 6 object kinds, a 2-state bundle lifecycle, and no transition engine, and it changed shape twice while this verification was running (events.js removed; Milestone/Plan/Run/Grant/Edge/Dispute dropped; content_hash renamed payload_hash; SubjectRef charset widened). Until Builder A declares a frozen revision, any conformance verdict is point-in-time only — which is why this harness pins a snapshot.

attack_surfaces.title: SubjectRef charset widened to include '@' without protocol review
attack_surfaces.detail: user:alice@evil is now a valid principal. Visual spoofing of email-like principal ids becomes representable in signed objects.

attack_surfaces.title: Economic invariants absent from every delivered layer
attack_surfaces.detail: total_amount != sum(outputs) parses; outputs are not bounded by any escrow notion; u64 nonce has no monotonicity. The A5/A7 principles (proof before payment, idempotent effects) currently rest entirely on undelivered engines.

attack_surfaces.title: proof_binding does not bind milestone_id (R9): cross-milestone proof replay
attack_surfaces.detail: proof_binding = H(intent_hash || milestone_revision || evidence_root || policy_hash) has no milestone_id in the preimage, and the delivered proofBinding() API cannot even receive one. Two distinct milestones sharing revision/intent/policy/evidence-root therefore share a single binding: a VALID decision for milestone A is a structurally valid proof for milestone B. Commander ruling R9 requires binding milestone_id in V1.

attack_surfaces.title: Delivered settlement authorization is decision-gated on the superseded wire
attack_surfaces.detail: The frozen contract (docs/TRUST-CHAIN.md @ e28a22e) makes Settlement receipt-gated: outcome_receipt_hash required, decision_id/proof_binding forbidden. The delivered SettlementInstructionSchema still REQUIRES decision_id + proof_binding and has no outcome_receipt_hash slot, so the old decision-only authority remains structurally representable — a raw verifier assertion can drive settlement, violating the Proof Before Payment boundary (frozen principle 2).

attack_surfaces.title: settlement_key implements the superseded preimage (no domain prefix, proof_binding-keyed)
attack_surfaces.detail: The frozen idempotency key is SHA256("intent-protocol/v1/settlement-key" || 0x00 || outcome_receipt_hash[32] || UTF8(escrow_ref) || 0x00 || nonce_u64be[8]); the delivered settlementKey computes SHA256(proof_binding[32] || escrow_id || 0x00 || nonce) — no domain separation and keyed on the wrong authority object. Keys derived by the frozen formula and the delivered formula disagree for identical effects, so any cross-implementation idempotency check splits into two incompatible key universes until Builder A lands the frozen derivation.
